solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exceptionally peculiar English copper doing a bunk now

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the usual order, so the letters of peculiar are rearranged
doing a bunk is British slang for running off, so these letters leave the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A strange English policeman is on the run at this moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, Cu. Take E and CU out of PECULIAR, leaving PLIAR, and rearrange. 'Now' works because the puzzle appeared in that month.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter treats the current month of publication as the present, a topical definition by reference to the date.

clue.text: Organic compound contaminated iced tea brought round in the morning

indicators.note: the jumbled drink is brought round, enclosing the time-of-day abbreviation
something contaminated has been spoiled or messed up, so the letters of iced tea are jumbled

parts.note: am (ante meridiem) means in the morning

explanation.surface: A chemist warns that an iced tea delivered in the morning has been tainted with some chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contaminated' jumbles ICED TEA into ACETIDE, and 'brought round' puts that around AM.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the amide of acetic acid, a crystalline substance made of carbon, so it is an organic compound.

clue.text: Chemical fissure which gets filled in with time

indicators.note: the crack is filled, so the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split, so a fissure
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A chemical that seeps into a crack and fills it over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used in a laboratory to cause or detect a reaction is a chemical.

clue.text: Look round territory, mostly plain

indicators.note: the word for look goes round the shortened territory

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look!

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: land is territory

explanation.surface: Survey the area around you, which is largely flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' gives the old exclamation LO, and 'mostly' trims the last letter from the territory word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassy plain in South America, so it is a geographical synonym.

clue.text: WC Fields originally taken the wrong way as twit

indicators.note: taking it the wrong way means reading the letters backwards

parts.note: a WC is a lavatory, a loo

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of Fields

explanation.surface: A comedian, W C Fields, being misunderstood and treated as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: W C Fields was an American film comedian, but here WC is a toilet. LOO plus F, turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly, foolish person, an idiot or simpleton.

clue.text: Soldiers in an old company may be seen running through South America

definitions.text: may be seen running through South America

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops in a historic company may be spotted marching across South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is about a river, not marching troops.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a great river of Venezuela and Colombia, and rivers are said to run through a land.

clue.text: BBC boss hiding in shelter — a rocky situation

indicators.note: the boss is hiding inside the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
the head of the BBC is its Director-General, DG

explanation.surface: A BBC chief takes cover, in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rocky situation' sounds like trouble but is literal: a narrow shelf on a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shelf projecting from a cliff is a place, or situation, found on rock.

clue.text: Brings together old canoeists for reunion

indicators.note: a reunion brings things back together in a new order, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A gathering of former canoeing club members for a reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite or combine several things into one whole is to bring them together.

clue.text: Something put into food that's 'moreish', not cold

indicators.note: not cold means the letter for cold is left out

parts.note: moreish, British slang for food so tasty you want more, means addictive
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An ingredient that makes a dish moreish but is not served chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moreish' is everyday British for food you can't stop eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavouring, preservative or colouring added to food during manufacture.

clue.text: Noah so demanding about non-matching agricultural pair

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Noah insists on animals in pairs, yet frets about a pair that doesn't match.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah's ark took matching pairs; this pair is a farmer and his sheepdog, from the song 'One man went to mow' and a long-running BBC sheepdog trials programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer and his sheepdog are a working farm team of two, one human and one canine, hence unmatched.

clue.text: Cabbages and bits of lettuce perhaps voiced in song

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out, so the letters entered match the sound of the phrase

parts.words: Cabbages and bits of lettuce perhaps
parts.note: cabbages are greens, and bits of lettuce are leaves, said together

explanation.surface: A salad of cabbage and lettuce celebrated in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, GREENS and LEAVES give the old English ballad's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Tudor ballad, traditionally credited to Henry VIII, is a well-known English folk tune.

clue.text: Jack or one of a dozen others getting accommodation in the Home Counties?

definitions.text: Jack or one of a dozen others

indicators.note: the lodging goes inside the region abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE
a pad is slang for a flat or place to live

explanation.surface: A man named Jack, or one of twelve others, finding a home near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London. Jack is a playing card: a suit has thirteen cards, so the jack and twelve others.
explanation.definitionFit: Every card in one suit of a pack belongs to that suit, so the jack or any of its twelve suitmates qualifies.

clue.text: Cool genie, magical, from an age long gone

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A laid-back genie, working magic from ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological epoch of the Tertiary period, some 34 to 23 million years ago, is a time long past.

clue.text: Spear carried by Matabele is terrifying

indicators.note: the word is carried inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A warrior's spear is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Matabele, or Ndebele, are a people of southern Africa, which makes 'Spear' look like a war weapon; it is a fishing spear.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pronged spear used for catching fish, especially salmon.

clue.text: Most neglected and filthy places circumvented by track

indicators.note: circumvented means surrounded, so the dirty places lie inside the track

parts.note: a rut is a track worn by wheels
sties are pigsties, proverbially filthy

explanation.surface: Dirty, run-down spots that a road bypasses are the most neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron left unused corrodes, so the superlative of rusty means most neglected or out of practice.

clue.text: Leg muscle's first thing seen in country fellow of great strength

indicators.note: the leg and muscle letters are seen inside the country

parts.note: Iran is a country
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON

indicators.note: the first thing of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A strongman displays his leg muscle in a rural setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like the countryside but is a nation. In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of exceptional toughness and endurance, as in the gruelling triathlon or the superhero.

clue.text: One chum engaging another to concoct a plot

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so one friend encloses the other

parts.note: a mate is a chum
china is another chum, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate for mate

explanation.surface: One friend recruits another to hatch a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so 'china' is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scheme or devise secret plans is to plot, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Increases enclosures by river

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the river comes alongside the enclosures

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
pens are enclosures for animals

explanation.surface: A farmer adds more animal pens beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To make deeper or more intense is to increase, so the verb fits the intensifying sense.

clue.text: Scuffle with a thousand coming out about tax being put up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened scuffle goes round the tax
coming out means leaving, so the letter for a thousand is removed

parts.note: a melee is a confused scuffle or brawl
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: A brawl over raising taxes, with a thousand people storming out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' removes M, the Roman thousand, leaving ELEE; VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or lift something higher is to put it up.

clue.text: The criminal in charge, gangster to become moral

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: Al Capone is the gangster crosswords call AL

explanation.surface: A crook in charge, a mobster, turning straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being principled and right in conduct is the same as being moral.

clue.text: Place with famous parsonage and hospital having a valuable quality

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
worth is value or merit

explanation.surface: A village with a well-known vicarage and a hospital, a place of real value.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire village was home to the Brontë sisters, whose father's parsonage is now a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Yorkshire village is known for the Brontë family's rectory, now a museum.

clue.text: Fiddling with metal object with security devices attached? Not unknown

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: not unknown says the unknown letter is left out

parts.note: a key ring is an object with keys, security devices, attached to it
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Messing about with a metal gadget fitted with locks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags keys as 'security devices'. In algebra x, y and z are unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Making small, aimless adjustments to something is fiddling with it.

clue.text: Claws making mover unlikely to hurry, beginning to end

indicators.note: the beginning letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: a snail is the proverbial slow mover

explanation.surface: Claws on a slow-moving creature, from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' moves the S of SNAIL to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny tips on fingers and toes, or an animal's talons, are claws.

clue.text: Good tirade makes one yield

parts.note: a rant is a long angry speech, a tirade

explanation.surface: A decent outburst makes someone give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede or allow something, as in granting a point, is to yield.

clue.text: Sound correct — it's what an author must do

indicators.note: sound tells us the entry is said like the word for correct

parts.note: right means correct

explanation.surface: Getting it right is the author's duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors produce books and articles by composing words on the page, their essential task.

clue.text: The way someone may get 'screwed up'?

definitions.text: The way someone may get 'screwed up'?

parts.words: The way someone may get 'screwed up'?
parts.note: screwed up suggests being messed up, but here it means climbing upward in a corkscrew path, a way being a route

explanation.surface: How a person ends up emotionally messed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screwed up' sounds like distress; literally it is turning round and round like a screw while going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A helical flight of steps winds upward around a central post, so climbers rise as a screw thread does.

clue.text: Vehicle is guided — one lost

indicators.note: one lost means the letter for one disappears

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
led means guided

explanation.surface: A vehicle being steered, with one passenger missing.
explanation.walkthrough: IS LED loses I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh or sledge running on snow is a vehicle without wheels.

clue.text: Lake in middle of Cheltenham enveloping a house

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping around, so the central letters surround the rest
the middle of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A lake in central Cheltenham surrounding a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham, a spa town in Gloucestershire, has ten letters, so its middle is TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California–Nevada border.
